text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The council of provincial governors reviewed at its meeting yesterday the military decree toughening the penalties for violations of building and demolition regulations. It also discussed simplifying the procedures for obtaining licences and reducing the fees for them.

- Rescue workers continued for the fifth day removing the rubble from the building which collapsed in Heliopolis. The Japanese team has dug 20 metres deep and has recorded heart beats at that depth. The number of bodies recovered has reached 39 and the head of the Japanese team said it has located 28 dead bodies under the rubble.
- President Hosni Mubarak continued his tour of South Sinai province. Yesterday he inspected Sharm el-Sheikh town.
- Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will today discuss the latest developments in the Palestinian-Israeli negotiations on redeployment in Hebron.
- Mubarak received a phone call yesterday evening from Israeli President Ezer Weizman and they discussed the negative effects of the difficulties in the peace process.

- The U.S. ambassador to Israel, Martin Indyk, said the U.S. administration appreciates the pioneering role of President Mubarak in the peace process and considers relations between Egypt and Israel the cornerstone of stability in the region.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, as deputy military commander, issued a militray decree yesterday to deter violations of building regulations and the deal with the phenomenon of collapsing buildings.
- The number of victims of the building which collapsed in Heliopolis has risen to 40 and the search continues.
- Trains have started running between the New Valley and Qena. The 240-km journey takes six hours.
- Military decree toughening the penalties for violating building regulations. Ten years' hard labour if the violation causes the death of someone or if three are injured.
- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi has ordered an inquiry into allegations that the police harassed journalists covering the building which collapsed in Heliopolis.

- The Supreme State Security Court in Cairo sentenced two men to death for the murder of a police general in Qena province. Three men were sentenced to life imprisonment, three to 15 years' hard labour and three to hard labour for periods ranging from five to 10 years. Seven were acquitted.
